findings.summary: DSPy provides multiple optimizer types with different trade-offs: few-shot bootstrapping, coordinate ascent, Bayesian discrete search, and stochastic mini-batch approaches.
findings.raw_excerpt: BootstrapFewShot (teacher-generated demos, metric-validated). BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch (multiple attempts, 50+ examples). COPRO (coordinate ascent hill-climbing for instructions). MIPROv2 (3-stage: bootstrap traces, grounded proposals, Bayesian discrete search, 40+ trials 200+ examples). SIMBA (stochastic mini-batch, targets high-variability examples, self-reflective improvement rules). GEPA (trajectory reflection, domain feedback integration). BetterTogether (sequences prompt and weight optimization).

findings.summary: DSPy optimizers typically cost around $2 and require approximately 10 minutes to run.
findings.raw_excerpt: Typical cost $2, ~10 minutes.

findings.summary: PromptBreeder employs multiple mutation strategies including LLM paraphrasing and edit operators for structural transformation.
findings.raw_excerpt: PromptBreeder mutation operators: LLM paraphrasing, edit operators (swap/drop/clarify), structural rewrites.

findings.summary: PromptBreeder uses multiple selection mechanisms including elitism, roulette-wheel selection, softmax-based fitness ranking, and UCB-based exploration-exploitation.
findings.raw_excerpt: Selection: elitism, roulette-wheel, softmax over fitness, UCB exploration-exploitation.

findings.summary: PromptBreeder recommends population size 20-50, generations 10-30, with mutation pool of 5-20 candidates.
findings.raw_excerpt: Population size 20-50, generations 10-30, mutation pool 5-20.

findings.summary: PromptBreeder implements four crossover mechanisms: single-point, uniform, section-wise, and clause-level swapping.
findings.raw_excerpt: Crossover: single-point, uniform, section-wise, clause-level swapping.

findings.summary: PromptBreeder uses reflective modules with exponential smoothing alpha parameter 0.7-0.9 and maintains long-term reflection memory.
findings.raw_excerpt: Reflective modules with smoothing alpha=0.7-0.9. Long-term reflection memory.

findings.summary: Turintech Artemis platform uses semantic genetic algorithms with LLM ensemble mutations to generate candidate variations.
findings.raw_excerpt: Semantic genetic algorithms with LLM ensemble mutations.

findings.summary: Turintech uses hierarchical evaluation with Local (GA for independent components) and Global (Bayesian for interacting components) optimization levels.
findings.raw_excerpt: Local (GA for independent components) + Global (Bayesian for interacting).

findings.summary: Turintech employs hierarchical evaluation with cheap filters followed by expensive benchmarks to manage cost.
findings.raw_excerpt: Hierarchical evaluation: cheap filters then expensive benchmarks.

findings.summary: Turintech Artemis reports improvement rates of 9.3-36.9% depending on baseline tuning quality and metric definition.
findings.raw_excerpt: Results 9.3-36.9% improvement.

findings.summary: Evolutionary optimization works best when baselines are poorly tuned and metrics are well-defined.
findings.raw_excerpt: Works best with poorly tuned baselines and well-defined metrics.

findings.summary: Turintech reports variable computation cost ranging from 9-671 hours depending on problem complexity and configuration.
findings.raw_excerpt: Cost varies 9-671 hours.

findings.summary: MIPROv2 uses a three-stage approach: bootstrap traces for diversity, grounded proposals for relevance, and Bayesian discrete search for optimization.
findings.raw_excerpt: MIPROv2 (3-stage: bootstrap traces, grounded proposals, Bayesian discrete search, 40+ trials 200+ examples).

findings.summary: MIPROv2 generates 40+ trials across 200+ examples during its optimization process.
findings.raw_excerpt: 40+ trials 200+ examples

findings.summary: BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch generates 50+ examples during optimization exploration.
findings.raw_excerpt: BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch (multiple attempts, 50+ examples).

findings.summary: SIMBA targets high-variability examples for mutation, focusing optimization effort where uncertainty is highest.
findings.raw_excerpt: SIMBA (stochastic mini-batch, targets high-variability examples, self-reflective improvement rules).

findings.summary: COPRO uses coordinate ascent hill-climbing for instruction optimization, which is subject to local optima and plateau challenges.
findings.raw_excerpt: COPRO (coordinate ascent hill-climbing for instructions).

findings.summary: GEPA integrates domain feedback and trajectory reflection to guide optimization decisions.
findings.raw_excerpt: GEPA (trajectory reflection, domain feedback integration).

findings.summary: BetterTogether sequences prompt and weight optimization in a coordinated manner rather than treating them independently.
findings.raw_excerpt: BetterTogether (sequences prompt and weight optimization).

cross_references.relationship: Both implement stochastic mini-batch and gradient-based selection strategies, though DSPy SIMBA targets high-variability examples while PromptBreeder uses roulette-wheel and UCB mechanisms
Both platforms provide multiple optimizer types with hierarchical evaluation; DSPy uses Bayesian discrete search while Turintech uses ensemble mutations with local GA and global Bayesian search
Both use genetic algorithm foundations with population-based search; PromptBreeder emphasizes reflective modules while Turintech emphasizes semantic mutations and hierarchical filtering

gaps.description: No specific convergence criteria or stopping conditions for PromptBreeder iterations
DSPy documentation does not provide guidance on avoiding overfitting in optimization procedures
Turintech cost model details and how computational cost relates to problem size/complexity
Specific hyperparameter tuning strategies for PromptBreeder smoothing alpha and mutation pool sizes
DSPy guidance on how to detect and escape local optima in COPRO's coordinate ascent

metadata.processing_notes: All three cached sources successfully processed. dspy-optimizers.txt contained comprehensive catalog of 7 optimizer types with architectural patterns and cost metrics. promptbreeder.txt provided detailed mutation operators, selection strategies, and population parameters. turintech-evolutionary.txt described hierarchical evaluation architecture and reported effectiveness metrics. Cross-references identified shared concepts (genetic algorithms, hierarchical search, ensemble mutations) across platforms. Gaps identified in convergence criteria, overfitting prevention strategies, and detailed cost modeling.
